learning_outcomes.text: Systematic knowledge and understanding of the fundamentals of fluid mechanics: principles, equations, methods, and fundamental results from the chapters: physical properties, theory of fluid motion and deformation, fundamental equations of fluid mechanics, fluid statics, fluid dynamics (isochoric flows).
Knowledge and understanding of the theoretical bases of: a) methods for solving standard fluid mechanics problems; b) measuring the main parameters in fluid mechanics.

Ability to analyze standard fluid mechanics problems: problem framing, identification of phenomena and process conditions, particularization of fundamental equations, selection of the appropriate solution method.

Ability to solve standard fluid mechanics problems (statics, kinematics, dynamics) that: a) are reducible to equations or systems of equations with exact analytical solutions; or b) are reducible to the application of balance equations on standard control volumes - the case of isochoric and steady flows.
Knowledge of the main apparatus and measurement methods used in experimental fluid mechanics.
Ability to design and execute standard experimental fluid mechanics works, to process and interpret experimental results.
The discipline contributes to the development of transferable skills in the following three directions: Opinion formation (analysis and decision), Communication and teamwork, Continuous training.

syllabus_topics: Physical properties of fluids. General notions about fluids. Physical properties of liquids and gases. Cavitation.

Fluid statics. Definition of the object of fluid statics. Forces acting on fluids at rest. Hydrostatic pressure. Equations of fluid rest. Fundamental relation of hydrostatics. Consequences of the fundamental relation of hydrostatics. Fundamental relation of fluid statics in a gravitational field.

Action of fluids at rest on solid walls. Hydrostatic pressure forces on plane surfaces. Hydrostatic pressure forces on curved surfaces. Case of the action of liquids at rest on closed curved surfaces. Archimedes' principle.
Fluid kinematics. Elements of fluid motion. Theorem of quantity of motion, theorem of angular momentum.
Dynamics of ideal fluids. Equations of motion. Law of conservation and transformation of energy in the case of perfect fluid motion (Bernoulli's relation).

Laminar flow of real fluids. Equations of motion of real fluids. Law of conservation and transformation of energy in the case of laminar flow of real fluids (Bernoulli's relation). Flows with negligible inertial forces. Laminar flow in straight circular pipes.

Calculation of hydraulic resistances. General expressions for calculating hydraulic resistances. Notion of roughness. Calculation of linear hydraulic resistances. Practical diagrams for calculating the coefficient of linear head losses. Local hydraulic resistances.
Calculation of pressure pipes. Definitions, classification and general problems of pressure pipe calculation. Short pipes; the siphon. Long pipes. Unsteady flow in pressure pipes.
Problems solved by fluid mechanics methods specific to Mechanical Engineering specialization.
Laboratory presentation. Processing of occupational safety and health norms.
Pressure measurement. Determination of the accuracy class of a manometer.
Measurement of water flow with a diaphragm flowmeter.
Determination of the linear loss coefficient for a steel pipe and its dependence on the Re number.
Determination of the local resistance coefficient for a globe valve.
Tracing of the energy and piezometric lines.
